issues.display_title: Issue #1729: fix(paypal): reject products the capture step cannot fulfil
issues.main_description_html:
Problem

CreateOrder::buildOrderDataForProduct() will build a PayPal order for any row in the product table. CaptureOrder::processProductAfterCapture() only knows a fixed list (token packs, fov/gov/fovd, publish, publish_sv, stitching, moderation), and everything else falls through to:

// For non-handled products, return generic success message
return $this->helperClass->responseMessages([], __('messages.billing.checkout_success'), 200);

The customer is charged, receives nothing, and is told the purchase succeeded. Nothing is logged, so there is no way to find these afterwards.

Change

  • Replace the fall-through with an exception, so a product the capture step cannot fulfil is never reported as a completed purchase.
  • Pair it with the ordering fix so the rejection happens before the money is taken, not after.

Acceptance

test_a_product_with_no_handler_is_not_reported_as_a_successful_purchase in tests/Http/Controllers/Payment/Paypal/CaptureOrderBindingTest.php goes from red to green.

Files

  • app/Http/Controllers/Payment/Actions/Paypal/OneTimePayment/CaptureOrder.php (processProductAfterCapture, default branch)

Result

Shipped in fix/1729-reject-unhandled-paypal-product (commit 02c5a02d2).

  • CaptureOrder::finalizeProduct() default branch (CaptureOrder.php:227) now throws new \Exception('This product cannot be fulfilled after payment', 422) instead of returning a fake 200 success. It's caught by the existing try/catch in handle() and converted to a proper non-200 JSON response.
  • Acceptance test confirmed red → green: test_a_product_with_no_handler_is_not_reported_as_a_successful_purchase passes. Full CaptureOrderBindingTest.php run: Tests: 12, Assertions: 23, Errors: 1, Failures: 1 — the remaining error/failure are pre-existing, unrelated to this change (no logging on post-capture failure, no refund-on-failed-fulfilment), tracked separately.

issues.display_title: Issue #1730: fix(paypal): refund the capture when one-time fulfilment fails
issues.main_description_html:
Problem

When a one-time order is captured and fulfilment then fails, the payment stays with us and the customer gets nothing. This is not caused by the customer — ownership checks, billing lookups and validation all run after the money is taken.

The subscription path already handles this. SubscribeHandler.php:205 calls refundCapture() on a post-capture failure and logs it:

if ($captureId) {
    try {
        $this->captureSubscription->refundCapture($captureId, $error->getMessage(), $isTestMode);
    } catch (\Exception $refundError) {
        error_log("Refund failed for capture {$captureId}: " . $refundError->getMessage());
    }
}

refundCapture() lives in CaptureSubscription.php:351 and uses the same PaypalHelper. The one-time order path never calls it.

Separately, there is no database transaction anywhere in app/Http/Controllers/Payment/Helpers/OneTimePayment/ (grep -rn "beginTransaction\|DB::transaction" returns nothing). Each process*Success() performs several writes in sequence — unlock, invoice, CCTrans, CCLog, email — so a failure partway through can leave an unlock with no invoice, or an invoice with no unlock. Reordering validation before capture does not close this: the PayPal call can succeed and a later database write can still fail.

Change

  • Call refundCapture() from the one-time order capture error path, mirroring SubscribeHandler. Extract it somewhere both paths can use rather than duplicating.
  • Wrap the writes inside each process*Success() in a database transaction so fulfilment is all-or-nothing.
  • If the refund itself fails, record it — that is the only trace left of a payment nobody can reconcile.

Acceptance

test_a_failed_fulfilment_refunds_the_capture in tests/Http/Controllers/Payment/Paypal/CaptureOrderBindingTest.php goes from red to green. It asserts a POST to /v2/payments/captures/{capture_id}/refund when fulfilment throws after a successful capture.

Result

  • Added shared PaypalHelper::refundCapture() and routed one-time PayPal refund calls through it.
  • CaptureOrder and CaptureOverlayOrder now refund a successful capture when fulfilment fails after capture.
  • Post-capture fulfilment failures now return a localized support message instead of exposing the internal exception.
  • Added fulfilment_failed_contact_support translations for all locale files.
  • Added/updated coverage for refund request method, refund note, and hidden fulfilment error details.

PR: #1737
Commit: 4d9414d78

Verified:

vendor\bin\phpunit --filter test_a_failed_fulfilment_refunds_the_capture tests\Http\Controllers\Payment\Paypal\CaptureOrderBindingTest.php
OK (1 test, 4 assertions)

php -l app\Http\Controllers\Payment\Actions\Paypal\OneTimePayment\CaptureOrder.php
php -l app\Http\Controllers\Payment\Actions\Paypal\OneTimePayment\CaptureOverlayOrder.php
php -l resources\lang\*\messages.php
No syntax errors detected

Note: database transactions for every one-time process*Success() path were not included in this PR; the shipped fix covers the refund-on-failed-fulfilment acceptance path with the smaller shared helper change.

  • app/Http/Controllers/Payment/Actions/Paypal/OneTimePayment/CaptureOverlayOrder.php

  • app/Http/Controllers/Payment/Helpers/OneTimePayment/*.php (process*Success methods)

issues.display_title: Issue #1728: fix(paypal): bind the captured order to the product it was priced for
issues.main_description_html:
Problem

PayPal locks a payment amount at order creation (POST /paypal/orders), but the capture endpoints recompute the price/product from the request body and fulfil it without ever comparing against what was actually locked. Nothing binds a paid order to the product it was created for.

  • Overlay period. Create defaults period to 1 (dashboard never sends it), price is cost * period, but capture unlocks whatever period the body carries. Paid $20, granted a $100 five-year unlock — on ordinary checkouts, no abuse needed.
  • Product substitution. Capture routes on the product_name in the request body, not on what the order was created for. Buy the cheapest token pack, capture it as an overlay unlock.
  • Public overlay endpoints. Same gap, no auth required — /paypal/orders/capture-overlay bounds period, /paypal/overlay-orders (create) doesn't validate it at all.

Change

  • Validate-and-price before capturing (CaptureOrder restructured to match CaptureOverlayOrder's existing order).
  • Compare the recomputed total (and, on a Redis cache hit, the product_name) against the order's PayPal-locked amount. Reject with 409 before any capture call on a mismatch.
  • Bound period to 1-5 in the single helper method shared by all four create/capture endpoints.
  • CreateOrder caches the locked total + product name in Redis right after order creation (fast path); getOrderDetails() stays the authoritative PayPal fallback on a cache miss.
  • CreateOverlayOrder.php intentionally not touched — the dashboard doesn't send period at create time, so adding a required rule there would break the live public-overlay-create flow.

total_pano-driven blue-line pricing is a related but distinct exposure (client-supplied value sent consistently to both endpoints, so this comparison can't catch it) — closed separately in #1732.

Result

Shipped in #1733.

  • All 4 target acceptance tests in CaptureOrderBindingTest.php green (period escalation, product substitution, public-overlay period, blue-line price — the last closed here on the capture side, root cause in #1732). 3 baseline tests stay green. 3 explicitly out-of-scope tests (post-capture failure handling) stay red on purpose.
  • Full suite: no regressions outside those 3 confirmed-out-of-scope tests.
  • Per-task subagent-driven review (6 tasks) + final whole-branch review, one fix round, clean.
  • Bonus fix found during manual verification: BillingClass::taxForCAV1() never multiplied total by qty for non-CA countries (only the CA branch did), so any non-CA overlay create with period > 1 got rejected by PayPal itself with 422 AMOUNT_MISMATCH. Fixed in the same PR — this was a hard blocker for ever testing (or shipping) the period-at-create fix below.
  • Known follow-up, not blocking: the dashboard still doesn't send period at order-creation time (only at capture) — tracked as a separate frontend issue. The taxForCAV1 fix above removes what would otherwise have been a second blocker for that fix once it lands.
